coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Smith Cardiovascular Research Building
record.summary: The five-story headquarters of the UCSF Cardiovascular Research Institute, a lab building with an outpatient clinic and a vivarium, opened in 2010; a May 2008 groundbreaking report and the contractors' own project descriptions give 232,000 sq ft, though the contractors' project-details box lists 323,000, so the size is not fully settled.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd in DataSF's parcel data) alone is about 12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

costs.what: Project budget of $254 million (to be funded from gifts $198 million, external financing $42 million and campus funds $14 million) in the capital budget amendment the UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings approved for presentation to the Board on November 13, 2007; Industrial Info Resources' May 14, 2008 report on the May 7, 2008 groundbreaking repeats '$254 million'. The contractor pages give a $196 million contract amount. A budget, not a construction cost or a final cost

milestones.text: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings holds a preliminary design review of the Mission Bay Cardiovascular Research Building; the campus reports it is expecting a $100 million cash gift and a matching $50 million gift (bringing the campus close to $180 million in gifts in hand; the minutes give no project budget) and plans to seek full design approval in November 2007

changes.text: Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape.

The Smith Cardiovascular Research Building's note now says two contractor pages describe a five-story, 232,000-square-foot building in their text but list 323,000 square feet in their details box, so the size is not settled. The $196 million they give is the construction contract amount, not the project's total cost.

The Smith Cardiovascular Research Building page now dates its $254 million to the Regents' November 13, 2007 budget amendment and calls it a budget. It also lists the contractors' conflicting sizes without the unreadable Architizer figures, and notes a six-level tag in OpenStreetMap.

changes.text: The Smith Cardiovascular Research Building's size now leads with 232,000 sq ft, as a 2008 groundbreaking report and its contractors' own descriptions give it; its $254 million cost now cites that readable 2008 report.

The record gave 236,000 sq ft and $254 million from an Architizer listing that could not be read; two readable contractor pages give 323,000 sq ft and a $196 million contract amount, so the record now states the conflict instead of one figure. The September 2007 Regents minutes give about $180 million in gifts in hand but no project budget, so the $254 million clause was removed from that milestone. The opening is 2010 without a month (UCSF's history gives the year only), and the aerial photo caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'.

open_questions: Exact opening month/day not confirmed by a primary source; a specific Nov 1, 2010 date found in one web-search summary was not traceable to a primary document, so it isn't used here.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.

The Regents' full budget and design approval for this project is in the Committee on Grounds and Buildings minutes of November 13, 2007 (item G): a $254 million budget and approval of the design, which the committee voted to present to the Board; the Board's own vote was not read. An earlier version of this note referred to a May 2008 Regents item amending the budget to $254 million; that item could not be located and is not used.

As of 2026-10-12, an Architizer listing could not be read (access refused), and the architect fact rests on it; two readable contractor pages (Tutor Perini; Rudolph and Sletten) name the architect as 'SmithGroupJJR' and Industrial Info Resources (May 14, 2008) says 'Designed by Detroit's SmithGroup'. Size is not settled: the same contractor pages describe a 'five-story, 232,000-square-foot' building but list 'SIZE 323,000 Square Feet' in their details box, and Industrial Info Resources gives 232,000; no source read explains the 323,000. The contractor pages also give completion 2010 and a $196 million contract amount, which differs from the $254 million budget shown in the costs.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the gross_sqft fact and summary reported the contractor pages as giving 323,000 sq ft, but those pages' own descriptions say 232,000 (323,000 is only in their details box), matching Industrial Info Resources' May 14, 2008 report of a 232,000-square-foot building. The $254 million cost, which rested only on an unreadable Architizer listing, now cites the same May 2008 report and is dated to it.

Gross floor area: Industrial Info Resources' groundbreaking report (May 14, 2008) and the project descriptions on two contractor pages (Tutor Perini; Rudolph and Sletten, both undated) call it a 'five-story, 232,000-square-foot' building; the same contractor pages' project-details box lists 323,000, and an Architizer listing (undated), which was not readable when checked, gives about 236,000.

Use of the building: the laboratories, outpatient clinic and top-floor vivarium are from Tutor Perini's project page (undated); an Architizer listing (undated), not readable when checked in September 2026, adds 'wet labs'.

record.notes: Five stories; size and cost conflict between sources: an Architizer listing credited to SmithGroup (which could not be checked in September 2026) gives ~236,000 sq ft and ~$254 million, while two contractor pages (Tutor Perini; Rudolph and Sletten) describe a 'five-story, 232,000-square-foot' building in their text but list 'SIZE 323,000 Square Feet' in their project-details box, so the size is not settled; the same two pages give a $196 million 'Contract Amount' (the construction contract, not the project's total cost). Headquarters of the UCSF Cardiovascular Research Institute (UCSF history: opening in 2010) with laboratories, an outpatient clinic and a vivarium. Architect per Architizer SmithGroup with Jim Jennings Architecture (landscape Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture); the contractor pages say SmithGroupJJR. Opened 2010 (year only; a specific Nov 1, 2010 date found in one search summary was not traceable to a primary document, so not used).
